before: An ordered room refused a change made before its last close only by its addresses: a close gave every item a new address, so an old address resolved to nothing and the room refused it as other-file. A room file that keeps the addresses would apply such a change, or an old log, a second time.
after: The document keeps the highest applied counter of each change id namespace, raised inside the change's undo record, so a refused change leaves it as it was and every copy holds the same counters. A room refuses a change, or a log entry, whose counter is at or under the one its file holds for the namespace, with the existing code other-file. A repeated id of the same file still gets its first order number. A session's change ids count on past the counter its document holds for its namespace, so a page that keeps its namespace across a reload or a close is not refused.
reason: Change messages, refusal messages, the change log and the Yjs format do not change: other-file is a refusal code every client already reads, and a client never sends a counter twice in one namespace. A room file of today's version holds no counters, so a room opened from it refuses nothing more. A room admits only clients of its own code version.
